items.eu-nis2::article-20: Cybersecurity is a board-level duty under NIS2's Article 20: the management body of an essential or important entity must approve the risk-management measures taken to comply with Article 21, oversee their implementation, and its members can be held liable for infringements. Management-body members must also follow training to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices, and entities are encouraged to offer similar training to employees regularly.
items.eu-nis2::article-21: NIS2's Article 21 requires essential and important entities to take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks to the security of their network and information systems, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents on service recipients and other services. Based on an all-hazards approach and the state of the art, the measures must include at least: risk-analysis policies, incident handling, business continuity (backup, disaster recovery, crisis management), supply-chain security, security in acquisition/development/maintenance including vulnerability handling, effectiveness-assessment policies, cyber hygiene and training, cryptography and encryption policies, HR security, access control and asset management, and multi-factor or continuous authentication with secured communications.
items.eu-nis2::article-23: Under NIS2's Article 23, essential and important entities must notify their CSIRT or competent authority of any incident with a significant impact on their services without undue delay: an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours with an initial assessment and, where available, indicators of compromise, and a final report within one month. Entities must also warn potentially affected service recipients of significant cyber threats and the measures available to them. An incident counts as significant where it caused or can cause severe operational disruption or financial loss, or considerable damage to other persons.
items.eu-nis2::article-32: Essential entities under NIS2 are subject to proactive supervision: NIS2's Article 32 equips competent authorities to carry out on-site and off-site inspections, regular and targeted security audits, ad hoc audits after a significant incident, security scans, and requests for information, documents, and evidence of implemented cybersecurity policies. Authorities can also issue warnings, binding instructions, orders to cease infringements, and orders to implement remedial actions. This is a duty on the authorities; it is carried here so the enforcement regime facing essential entities stays visible.
items.eu-nis2::article-33: Important entities under NIS2 are supervised reactively: NIS2's Article 33 triggers action through ex post supervisory measures when the authority is provided with evidence, indication or information of non-compliance - at least on-site inspections and off-site ex post supervision, targeted security audits, security scans, and requests for information, data, documents and evidence - together with enforcement powers such as warnings, binding instructions, orders to remedy or cease infringements, and orders to publicise aspects of infringements. The distinction from essential-entity supervision is when the regulator shows up, not whether the obligations apply.
items.eu-nis2::article-34: Where an essential or important entity infringes NIS2's Article 21 or 23, Member States must ensure that administrative fines can be imposed on top of the Article 32 or 33 supervisory and enforcement measures, calibrated to be effective, proportionate and dissuasive with the same assessment factors as the essential-entity safeguards. Essential entities face upper bounds of at least EUR 10 million or 2 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, and important entities at least EUR 7 million or 1,4 %; Member States may additionally levy periodic penalty payments to compel an entity to cease an infringement, and where national law lacks administrative fines, courts must impose equivalents.
items.eu-nis2::article-35: When a supervisory or enforcement action under NIS2 reveals that an entity's breach of its Article 21 or 23 obligations may also entail a personal-data breach notifiable under the GDPR, the competent authority must inform the competent data-protection supervisory authority without undue delay. Where the data-protection authority has already fined the same conduct under the GDPR, no additional NIS2 administrative fine may be imposed for that conduct, though the authority may still apply NIS2's supervisory and enforcement measures.
